summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old man with a history of alcoholic cirrhosis, chronic steroid-dependent asthma, and CMV gastritis was admitted for an acute asthma exacerbation and worsening epigastric pain following a recent alcohol binge. He was treated with BiPAP, intravenous steroids, and nebulizers, with gradual improvement in respiratory status. His abdominal pain was attributed to a flare of CMV gastritis, and he was restarted on valganciclovir. Alcohol withdrawal was monitored with CIWA, though symptoms were mild. He was discharged on a prednisone taper, atovaquone for PCP prophylaxis, and continued valganciclovir. Follow-up was arranged with pulmonology, sleep medicine, and hepatology for ongoing management of asthma, possible sleep apnea, and a liver nodule noted on prior imaging. He committed to sobriety and medication adherence.
